subject.title: fix #95895: [Security]: GEMINI_API_KEY written as a plaintext literal in the generated systemd service unit

question: Should OpenClaw accept file-backed EnvironmentFile rendering for the known Google/Gemini auth-profile env refs while leaving other auth-profile env refs on the existing inline path?
rationale: The mechanics are small and source-backed, but this changes how installed services receive provider credentials and CI cannot decide the intended security and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Accept Narrow Google/Gemini Policy
options.body: Merge this PR after current-head gates are acceptable if maintainers agree the existing EnvironmentFile contract is the right boundary for these Google/Gemini auth-profile keys.

options.title: Request Generic Auth-Profile Policy
options.body: Ask for a revised patch if all safe auth-profile env refs should use one shared file-backed policy instead of a Google/Gemini allowlist.

options.title: Pause For Separate Security Work
options.body: Keep this PR paused or close it only if maintainers want the linked security issue limited to config SecretRefs and plan auth-profile handling elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Google/Gemini Policy
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after current-head gates are acceptable if maintainers agree the existing EnvironmentFile contract is the right boundary for these Google/Gemini auth-profile keys.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current-main config SecretRef repair for the same issue and are the strongest evidenced owner for this specific credential-rendering boundary.
